subsection.name: Prerequisites
subsection.p: Before starting, ensure you have the following installed:

ul.li: Web Browser (Chrome / Firefox / Edge to check compatibility)

subsection.name: Repository Setup and first build
subsection.h4: Clone the HtmlUnit repository from GitHub
Compile the project to ensure everything is working correctly
subsection.p: Do not run the whole test suite because it takes a significant amount of time.

subsection.name: Eclipse Project Setup
subsection.p: Use the Maven Eclipse Plugin to generate Eclipse project files with source downloads:
Then import the project into Eclipse:

p.code: File → Import → Existing Projects into Workspace

subsection.p: Usually you would run only select tests from Eclipse.
Please refer to the section Running Tests with real browsers below for more options.

subsection.name: IntelliJ IDEA Project
subsection.p: IntelliJ IDEA has built-in Maven support and can directly import the HtmlUnit project.

ol.li: Navigate to the cloned HtmlUnit directory
Select the pom.xml file and click Open
Choose Open as Project when prompted
IntelliJ will automatically detect the Maven project and import it

subsection.p: IntelliJ IDEA will automatically download dependencies and set up the project structure.

subsection.name: Running the Tests from Maven
subsection.p: Running the full test suite requires significant time (several hours) and resources. Therefore, several profiles are defined to run different parts of the test suite. These profiles are also used by the various Jenkins jobs.

subsection.name: Running Tests with real browsers
subsection.p: The primary goal of HtmlUnit development is to provide the most accurate simulation possible of supported browsers. Since browsers are constantly evolving, test assumptions must adapt with every browser version update. Therefore, almost all tests are implemented in such a way that they can be executed with HtmlUnit as well as with supported real browsers (with the help of Selenium WebDriver).
This functionality is provided by the superclass org.htmlunit.WebDriverTestCase. Test execution can be switched accordingly with the help of a configuration file.
By default, all tests run with HtmlUnit, but this behavior can be changed by placing a property file named test.properties in the HtmlUnit root directory.
Sample (remove sections not matching your operating system):
subsection.source:
browsers=hu #browsers=hu-ff #browsers=hu-ff, hu-chrome #browsers=ff, chrome, edge
# Unix/Linux paths ff.bin=/usr/bin/firefox ff-esr.bin=/usr/bin/firefox-esr geckodriver.bin=/usr/bin/driver/geckodriver chrome.bin=/path/to/chromedriver edge.bin=/path/to/chromedriver
# Windows paths geckodriver.bin=C:\\path\\to\\geckodriver.exe ff.bin=C:\\path\\to\\Mozilla Firefox\\firefox.exe ff-esr.bin=C:\\path\\to\\Mozilla Firefox ESR\\firefox.exe chrome.bin=C:\\path\\to\\chromedriver.exe edge.bin=C:\\path\\to\\msedgedriver.exe
# optional autofix=false
subsection.p: A comma-separated list containing any combination of:

ul.li: hu (for HtmlUnit with all browser versions)
ff-esr (running tests using real Firefox ESR)
chrome.bin (mandatory if missing from PATH): Location of the ChromeDriver binary (see Chrome Driver downloads)
geckodriver.bin (mandatory if missing from PATH): Location of the GeckoDriver binary (see Gecko Driver Releases)
ff.bin (optional): Location of the Firefox binary (on Windows, use double backslashes)
ff-esr.bin (optional): Location of the Firefox ESR binary (on Windows, use double backslashes)
edge.bin (mandatory if missing from PATH): Location of the MicrosoftWebDriver binary (see Microsoft Edge WebDriver downloads)
autofix (optional): If true, attempts to automatically fix real browser expectations or add/remove @NotYetImplemented annotations (use with caution!)
